questions.question: A student monitors a population of snails and groups them based on whether they have a banded shell or an unbanded shell. What type of variation is this, and what is its defining characteristic?
options: Continuous variation, because shell patterns can change over the snail's lifetime depending on diet.
Discontinuous variation, because the snails fall into distinct, separate categories with no intermediate states.
Continuous variation, because there is an infinite range of band widths that can be measured.
Discontinuous variation, because the feature is only determined by the soil chemistry of their habitat.

questions.question: Why is the exact surface area of leaves on an oak tree classified as showing continuous variation rather than discontinuous variation?
options: Because leaf surface area can be grouped into small, medium, and large categories.
Because it is controlled by a single gene with two possible alleles.
Because leaf area can take any numerical value within a wide range, rather than fitting into distinct categories.
Because leaf area is completely unaffected by the amount of sunlight the tree receives.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a continuous variation feature in a plant and a discontinuous variation feature in a human?
options: Plant: Number of petals on a daisy; Human: Body mass
Plant: Height of a sunflower; Human: ABO blood group
Plant: Seed coat texture (wrinkled or smooth); Human: Height
Plant: Chlorophyll presence; Human: Skin colour

questions.question: A class wants to collect primary data to investigate variation in human hand span. To ensure the data is reliable and displays a continuous pattern, how should they measure and record it?
options: Group students into 'small', 'medium', and 'large' hands by visual inspection.
Measure the distance from the thumb tip to the pinky tip of a fully stretched hand to the nearest millimeter.
Classify hand span based on whether the student can palm a basketball or not.
Count the number of creases on the palm of the dominant hand.

questions.question: A biologist measures the body lengths of 150 adult frogs in a pond. Which type of graph is most appropriate to display the distribution of this continuous data, and why?
options: A bar chart with gaps, because each individual frog represents a distinct category.
A pie chart, because it shows the percentage of frogs of different species.
A histogram, because the data is continuous and should be grouped into continuous intervals without gaps between bars.
A line graph plotting length against time, because the frogs grow continuously over their lifespan.

questions.question: When plotting a histogram for the heights of 100 pea plants, which of the following rules must be followed to correctly represent the continuous nature of the data?
options: Leave equal spaces between the vertical bars to show that each plant is separate.
Plot the frequency of plants on the x-axis and the height categories on the y-axis.
Ensure the bars touch each other and represent continuous intervals of height, such as 10-14.9 cm and 15-19.9 cm.
Draw a single smooth line connecting each individual plant's raw height measurement.

questions.question: A histogram showing the birth mass of 1000 newborn puppies shows a bell-shaped curve. What does this shape tell us about the continuous variation of birth mass in this population?
options: Most puppies have either extremely low or extremely high birth masses, with very few in the middle.
Birth mass is a discontinuous feature with only three distinct, separate categories.
Most puppies have a birth mass near the average, with fewer puppies having extremely high or extremely low masses.
The birth mass of each puppy increases at a steady, linear rate as time goes on.

questions.question: The adult height of identical twins can sometimes differ by a few centimeters. Which statement best explains this observation?
options: Height is a discontinuous trait determined solely by a single gene that mutated in one twin.
Height is a continuous trait influenced by both genetic potential and environmental factors like nutrition during childhood.
Identical twins do not share any genetic material, so their heights are independent.
Environmental factors like exercise can change the underlying DNA sequence of the height genes.

questions.question: A student collects data on the natural eye colours of people in a theater. Why must this data be displayed using a bar chart with gaps between the bars?
options: Because eye colour is a continuous variable that can take any value.
Because eye colour is discontinuous, representing distinct, non-overlapping categories.
Because the gaps show that eye colour changes gradually as a person ages.
Because the total number of people surveyed is too small for a histogram.

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to show the frequency of different blood groups (A, B, AB, O) in a school class, which drafting decision is correct?
options: Merge the bars for A and AB because they share similar letters.
Place the blood group categories on the horizontal x-axis and leave gaps between the vertical bars.
Connect the top of each bar with a continuous line graph to show the trend.
Force the bars to touch to show that blood can be mixed during transfusions.

questions.question: You are analyzing a bar chart displaying the ability of students to roll their tongue (Rollers vs. Non-rollers). The chart has two tall, separate bars. What is the most accurate conclusion you can draw?
options: Most students are slowly learning how to roll their tongues over time.
Tongue rolling is a continuous trait with many intermediate levels of rolling ability.
The population is divided into two distinct groups, indicating tongue rolling is a discontinuous trait.
The environment has caused a gradual shift in the tongue-rolling capacity of the students.

questions.question: A person trains hard, eats a highly nutritious diet, and moves to a sunny climate. Which of their following features will remain completely unaffected by these lifestyle and environmental changes?
options: Their muscle mass
Their skin tone
Their ABO blood group
Their resting heart rate

questions.question: A pair of robins builds a nest and hatches eggs. Even though the chicks look very different from the adults at first, they grow up to be robins rather than blackbirds. Why does this occur?
options: Organisms always reproduce to make offspring of their same kind due to species resemblance.
The chicks learn to mimic the behavior of blackbirds if they share the same woodland.
The food provided by the parents chemically converts the chicks into robins.
Robins can choose which species of bird they want their offspring to become.

questions.question: A puppy is born with the floppy ears of its mother and the spotted coat pattern of its father. What biological concept does this pattern of features best demonstrate?
options: The puppy only inherits features from the male parent.
The puppy is a clone of its parents.
Offspring inherit genetic features from both parents, resulting in family resemblance.
The puppy's features are entirely shaped by the environment of the kennel.

questions.question: How are inherited features, such as natural hair color or lobed ears, physically passed from parents to their offspring during reproduction?
options: Through the transmission of learned behaviors during early childhood.
By passing DNA molecules containing genetic instructions from parents to offspring.
Through nutrients shared in the environment where the offspring grow.
By the physical restructuring of the offspring's cells to match the parent's cells.

questions.question: A green plant is grown in complete darkness. Over two weeks, its leaves turn yellow and its stem grows unusually long and thin. What does this demonstrate about plant features?
options: The plant has mutated its DNA to become a different species.
Some features are caused or modified by the organism's environment.
Light levels have no impact on the physical features of growing plants.
The plant is passing these newly acquired yellow leaves directly to its seeds.

questions.question: A cat gives birth to a litter of five kittens. They all have the same mother and father, yet some are black, some are ginger, and they have different temperaments. Why is this?
options: Sexual reproduction produces identical offspring unless mutations occur in every generation.
There is usually variation between offspring; they are not identical to their parents or to one another.
The kittens have different fathers because they were born at different times of the day.
Environmental temperature in the womb determines the coat colour of each individual kitten.

questions.question: Compare the differences between a German Shepherd dog and a Poodle dog, versus the differences between a German Shepherd dog and a Red Fox. What does this comparison illustrate?
options: Differences within a species (dogs) are greater than differences between different species (dog and fox).
Differences between different species (dog and fox) are greater than differences within the same species (dogs).
There are no measurable differences between individuals of the same species.
The German Shepherd is more closely related to the Red Fox than to the Poodle.

questions.question: When looking at a field of daisies, you notice some have slightly wider petals, some are taller, and some have pale pink edges. What is the scientific term for these differences among individuals of the same species?
options: Speciation
Adaptation
Variation
Evolution

questions.question: Which of the following human characteristics is determined solely by inherited genetic information in the genome and cannot be altered by lifestyle or environmental factors?
options: ABO blood type
Body mass
Scar tissue on skin
Spoken language accent

questions.question: A scientist is classifying different characteristics of a plant species. Which of the following features represents discontinuous variation because it falls into distinct, non-overlapping categories?
options: The concentration of chlorophyll in the leaves measured in mg/g.
The presence or absence of stripes on the flower petals.
The height of the stem at maturity.
The total surface area of the leaves.

questions.question: Why is the mass of a group of domestic rabbits classified as showing continuous variation rather than discontinuous variation?
options: Rabbit masses can only be represented by integers and have no intermediate values.
Rabbit masses are determined entirely by a single gene with two alleles.
Rabbit masses can take any numerical value within a range and do not fit into distinct categories.
Rabbit masses are fixed at birth and do not change throughout the rabbit's life.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a feature showing continuous variation with one showing discontinuous variation in humans?
options: Continuous: Eye colour; Discontinuous: Body mass
Continuous: Height; Discontinuous: ABO blood group
Continuous: Lobed or lobeless ears; Discontinuous: Hand span
Continuous: Biological sex; Discontinuous: Skin pigmentation

questions.question: A class of students wants to collect primary data to investigate discontinuous variation in their school. Which protocol would be most appropriate?
options: Measuring each student's height using a tape measure to the nearest millimetre.
Recording the exact time in seconds each student can hold their breath.
Surveying classmates to record who can and cannot roll their tongue into a U-shape.
Weighing school bags using a digital balance to find the average mass.

questions.question: Students have gathered data on the lengths of 150 oak leaves collected from a single tree. Why is a histogram or line graph, rather than a bar chart, the correct way to display this data?
options: Leaf length is a discontinuous variable with fixed categories.
Leaf length is a continuous variable that can take any value within a range, requiring a continuous scale.
A bar chart cannot display more than ten data points at a time.
Oak leaf length is purely determined by genetics and has no environmental influence.

questions.question: When plotting a histogram to show the continuous variation of plant heights in a garden, how should the data on the horizontal axis (x-axis) be structured?
options: Each individual plant should have its own separate, named bar.
The data must be grouped into continuous, equal-sized intervals (bins) with no gaps between them.
The heights should be listed from tallest to shortest with gaps between each distinct height value.
Only the minimum, maximum, and average heights should be plotted as three separate points.

questions.question: A histogram representing the heights of 200 adult sunflower plants shows a single, broad peak centered around 1.8 meters, with very few plants under 1.2 meters or over 2.4 meters. What is the most accurate interpretation of this graph?
options: There are two distinct, non-overlapping height categories of sunflowers in this population.
Sunflowers only grow to exactly 1.8 meters, and any other measurement is an experimental error.
The heights show continuous variation, with most plants clustered around an average height and fewer at the extremes.
The height of these sunflowers is determined by a single gene that prevents growth beyond 2.4 meters.

questions.question: Identical twin calves are separated at birth. Calf A is fed a nutrient-rich diet in a warm barn, while Calf B is fed a restricted diet in a cold, exposed field. As adults, Calf A has a much larger body mass than Calf B. What does this demonstrate about continuous variation?
options: Continuous variation is determined solely by the calves' identical genetic code.
Continuous variation is unaffected by lifestyle or environmental conditions like diet and temperature.
Continuous variation is usually influenced by a combination of genetics, environment, and lifestyle.
Environmental factors can completely alter an organism's species identity.

questions.question: A biologist is displaying data on the different blood groups (A, B, AB, and O) found within a population of chimpanzees. Why is a bar chart, with gaps between the bars, the most suitable choice for this data?
options: Blood group data is continuous and has infinite intermediate values.
Blood group data is discontinuous, meaning the categories are distinct and there are no intermediate values.
The biologist did not collect enough primary data to make a histogram.
Chimpanzee blood groups are determined entirely by environmental factors.

questions.question: When plotting discontinuous variation data, such as human eye colour, on a bar chart, which of the following rules must be followed?
options: The bars must touch each other to show that eye colours merge into one another.
The horizontal axis must show a continuous numerical scale from lowest to highest value.
The bars representing the distinct categories (e.g., Blue, Brown, Green) should have gaps between them.
The height of each bar must represent the age of the individuals surveyed.

questions.question: An analyst examines a bar chart displaying the frequency of four different leaf shapes found in a forest understory. The bars are labelled 'Ovate', 'Lanceolate', 'Lobate', and 'Cordate'. What can the analyst correctly conclude from this chart?
options: Leaf shape is a continuous variable because the leaves can be any intermediate length.
The leaf shapes are distinct categories of discontinuous variation, and the chart shows the frequency of each category.
The chart proves that environmental factors like sunlight are the sole cause of these leaf shapes.
Leaf shape changes gradually along a scale and cannot be grouped into discrete categories.

questions.question: A child is born with attached earlobes, which is a feature of discontinuous variation. Despite moving to a different climate and changing their diet as they grow up, their earlobes remain attached. Why is this?
options: Discontinuous variation is heavily influenced by changes in diet and physical activity.
Discontinuous variation usually has only a genetic cause and is not affected by environment or lifestyle.
The environment can only change discontinuous features during adulthood.
Earlobe shape is a continuous feature that takes many years to show environmental effects.

questions.question: When two golden retrievers mate, their offspring are always recognizable as golden retrievers rather than another dog breed or species. Which fundamental biological principle does this demonstrate?
options: Offspring inherit genetic material only from the female parent.
When organisms reproduce, they make offspring of the same kind (species resemblance).
Environmental factors prevent dogs from producing offspring with any variation.
Genetic mutation always makes offspring completely identical to their ancestors.

questions.question: A puppy has its mother's floppy ears but its father's coat colour. Why does the puppy show this family resemblance?
options: The puppy inherited all of its genes from its mother and none from its father.
The puppy's features were determined entirely by the environment in which it was raised.
Offspring inherit features from both parents, so they look similar to their parents and to one another.
Floppy ears and coat colour are acquired characteristics that the parents developed during their lifetime.

questions.question: How are inherited features, such as natural eye colour or blood group, physically transmitted from parents to their offspring?
options: Through nutrients passed in food during early development.
Through the transmission of DNA from parents to offspring during reproduction.
By offspring mimicking the physical movements and lifestyle of their parents.
Via hormones released into the shared environment of the family.

questions.question: Two genetically identical strawberry plants are grown in different conditions. Plant X is grown in nutrient-rich soil with plenty of sunlight, while Plant Y is grown in poor soil in the shade. Plant X grows many large strawberries, whereas Plant Y grows only a few small ones. What does this experiment demonstrate?
options: Strawberry size is determined solely by inherited DNA and cannot be altered.
Some features are caused or changed by an organism's lifestyle and environment.
Identical genetic information guarantees identical physical features regardless of the environment.
Plant Y has underwent a genetic mutation that changed its species.

questions.question: A cat gives birth to a litter of five kittens. Although they share the same parents, some kittens are black, some are ginger, and they have different patterns. What does this illustrate about reproduction?
options: Offspring are always exact genetic clones of the mother.
Environmental differences in the womb make offspring completely unrelated to each other.
There is usually variation between offspring; they are not usually identical to their parents or one another.
Kittens change their fur patterns as a lifestyle choice after birth.

questions.question: If you compare a domestic dog, a grey wolf, and a red fox, which statement about their differences is biologically correct?
options: The differences between individual domestic dogs (within-species variation) are greater than the differences between a dog and a red fox.
Differences between distinct species are greater than the differences within a single species.
All members of different species are physically identical, whereas members of the same species have vast differences.
There are no measurable physical differences between a domestic dog and a grey wolf.

questions.question: In a field of wild daisies, some flowers have 20 petals while others have 24 petals, even though they belong to the same species. What is the correct term for these differences among individuals of the same species?
options: Speciation
Mutation
Variation
Classification

questions.question: Which of the following human characteristics is caused only by inherited genetic information in the genome and cannot be altered by lifestyle or environment?
options: Body mass
ABO blood type
Skin tone after sun exposure
Physical fitness level

questions.question: Why is the ability to roll your tongue classified as a discontinuous variation rather than a continuous variation?
options: It can be changed by practicing over time.
People can either roll their tongue or they cannot, with no intermediate states.
It is influenced heavily by the climate a person lives in.
The trait changes gradually as a person grows older.

questions.question: A student measures the heights of all students in a class. Why is height considered a continuous variation?
options: Height is determined by a single gene and does not change after birth.
Height can only be measured in whole centimetres, meaning it fits into distinct categories.
Height can take any numerical value within a range, depending on the precision of the measuring tool.
Height is entirely determined by environmental factors like diet, with no genetic influence.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a discontinuous variation in plants and a continuous variation in animals?
options: Plant: Flower colour (e.g., purple or white); Animal: Body mass of a dog.
Plant: Height of a sunflower; Animal: Blood group of a cat.
Plant: Leaf surface area; Animal: Presence of horns in sheep.
Plant: Rate of photosynthesis; Animal: Number of legs on a spider.

questions.question: A group of students wants to collect primary data to investigate variation. Which method would be most appropriate for collecting reliable primary data on a continuous variation?
options: Asking classmates to write down whether they are 'tall', 'medium', or 'short' on a survey.
Using a standard tape measure to record the actual arm span of classmates to the nearest millimetre.
Looking up average heights of teenagers in different countries on an online database.
Counting the number of students who have blue eyes versus those who have brown eyes.

questions.question: Why is a histogram or line graph chosen to represent continuous data, such as human hand span, instead of a bar chart with separated bars?
options: Continuous data represents distinct categories that have no numerical relationship.
A histogram uses adjacent columns without gaps because the data is on a continuous scale.
Line graphs are only used when there is no genetic component to the variation.
Bar charts can only display qualitative descriptions like 'large' or 'small'.

questions.question: When plotting a histogram of student heights to show continuous variation, how should the data be organised on the horizontal (x) axis?
options: Individual names of students arranged in alphabetical order.
Discrete categories of height, such as 'under 1.5m' and 'over 1.5m', with gaps between them.
Continuous intervals or bins (e.g., 140–144 cm, 145–149 cm) with no gaps between adjacent bars.
The frequency of students who fall into each exact, individual height value.

questions.question: A histogram displaying the mass of newborn puppies shows a bell-shaped curve. What does this shape tell us about the continuous variation of puppy mass in this population?
options: Most puppies have a mass near the extreme ends, with very few in the middle.
The puppies are divided into two distinct, non-overlapping groups of light and heavy puppies.
Most puppies have a mass close to the average, with fewer puppies having extremely low or high masses.
The environment has had absolutely no effect on the birth weight of the puppies.

questions.question: Human height is a classic example of continuous variation. Which of the following best explains why human height shows such a wide range of values?
options: It is controlled by a single gene that is highly prone to mutations caused by the sun.
It is determined solely by a person's diet during early childhood, regardless of parental height.
It is influenced by many genes acting together, alongside environmental factors like nutrition and lifestyle.
It is completely unaffected by environmental factors and depends only on a single pair of alleles.

questions.question: When displaying data collected on the ABO blood groups of 100 students, why is a bar chart with gaps between the bars the most appropriate representation?
options: Blood groups represent continuous data that can take any value between group A and group O.
The blood groups are distinct categories, and the gaps show that there are no intermediate values.
Bar charts are only used when the data is influenced heavily by the school environment.
Gaps are needed because blood type changes as a student grows older.

questions.question: If you are plotting a bar chart to show the frequency of different lobed and lobeless ear types in a classroom, how should this be constructed?
options: Plot the ear types on the x-axis as separate bars with gaps between them, and the count on the y-axis.
Group the students by their height on the x-axis and plot ear type on the y-axis.
Plot a continuous line connecting the points representing 'lobed' and 'lobeless' ears.
Draw overlapping bars on the x-axis to show that ear type is a continuous variable.

questions.question: A bar chart shows the frequency of different eye colours in a population. If the bar for 'brown eyes' is three times higher than 'blue eyes', what can be correctly inferred?
options: Brown-eyed individuals live three times longer than blue-eyed individuals.
There are three times as many individuals with brown eyes as there are with blue eyes in this sample.
Eye colour is a continuous trait that changes gradually over three distinct stages.
Brown eyes are three times more affected by sunlight than blue eyes.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the causes of discontinuous variation, such as whether a person has naturally dimples or not?
options: It is usually determined only by genetic factors and is unaffected by lifestyle or environment.
It is heavily influenced by diet during infancy and can be lost through exercise.
It changes constantly throughout an individual's life depending on their stress levels.
It is caused by a combination of many genes and severe environmental changes.

questions.question: When two oak trees reproduce sexually, the resulting offspring grow into oak trees and not pine trees. What fundamental biological concept does this demonstrate?
options: Offspring of the same kind are produced because organisms reproduce to make offspring of their own species.
Environment has a stronger influence on species identity than genetic material.
Sexual reproduction always produces offspring that are exact clones of the maternal parent.
Plants do not have genetic variation and therefore always look identical.

questions.question: A puppy looks similar to both its mother and its father, but is not identical to either. Why does this family resemblance occur?
options: The puppy inherited all of its genes from the mother, but the father influenced its development after birth.
The puppy inherited genetic features from both parents, leading to a blend of characteristics from both.
The puppy copy-pasted its entire DNA sequence directly from the environment where the parents lived.
Both parents passed on identical sets of chromosomes, making the offspring a clone of both.

questions.question: Which mechanism is directly responsible for passing inherited features from parents to their offspring during reproduction?
options: The transfer of blood from the parents to the offspring.
The physical imitation of parental behaviours by the offspring.
The passing of DNA containing genetic instructions from parents to offspring.
The sharing of the same diet and climate in the family home.

questions.question: A houseplant is grown in a dark cupboard, causing its leaves to turn yellow and its stem to grow unusually long and thin. How is this variation best described?
options: It is an inherited genetic mutation caused by the lack of light.
It is a feature changed by the organism's environment and is not passed to offspring.
It is a discontinuous variation that cannot be reversed by changing the light levels.
It is a species-level difference showing the plant has evolved into a new species.

questions.question: A pair of non-identical twin cats are born in the same litter. One has black fur and the other has ginger fur. Why is there usually variation between offspring of the same parents?
options: Offspring are clones of only one parent, which changes depending on the birth order.
Each offspring inherits a unique combination of genetic information from the parents.
The mother cat changes her DNA sequence between the births of each kitten.
Environmental factors inside the womb are completely identical, causing different genes to disappear.

questions.question: Consider a Chihuahua, a Great Dane, and a Red Fox. Which statement correctly compares the differences between them?
options: The differences between the Chihuahua and the Great Dane are greater than the differences between either dog and the Red Fox.
The differences between the Chihuahua and the Red Fox are greater than the differences between the Chihuahua and the Great Dane.
There are no physical differences between a Chihuahua and a Great Dane because they belong to the same species.
Species differences are always smaller than the variation observed between siblings of the same parents.

questions.question: Two pine trees of the same species are growing in the same forest, but one is taller and has more branches than the other. What is the biological term for these differences between individuals of the same species?
options: Mutation
Speciation
Variation
Classification

questions.question: A dog loses a leg in an accident. Later in life, this dog has a litter of puppies. Why are all the puppies born with four legs?
options: The missing leg is an environmental variation and does not alter the genetic information passed to the offspring.
The puppies' genes automatically repaired themselves using environmental signals.
Only female injuries are inherited by offspring, whereas male injuries are not.
The missing leg is a discontinuous genetic variation that is recessive.

questions.question: A scientist is classifying variations in a population of ladybirds. She notes that some ladybirds have 2 spots, some have 7 spots, and some have 10 spots, with absolutely no ladybirds having fractional or intermediate spot numbers like 4.5. How should this feature be classified?
options: As continuous variation, because the number of spots can be counted numerically.
As discontinuous variation, because the feature falls into distinct, separate categories with no intermediates.
As environmental variation, because the number of spots is determined by the aphid population size.
As continuous variation, because there is a wide range of spot counts across different ladybird species.

questions.question: When measuring the exact leaf lengths of 100 oak trees, a student finds that the values range smoothly from 5.2 cm to 14.8 cm, including values like 7.34 cm and 11.05 cm. What type of variation does leaf length represent, and why?
options: Discontinuous variation, because leaf length can be grouped into small, medium, and large categories.
Discontinuous variation, because the maximum leaf length is limited by the tree's age.
Continuous variation, because the feature can take any numerical value within a continuous range.
Continuous variation, because leaf lengths are identical across all branches of a single tree.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a human feature and a plant feature with their correct type of variation?
options: Discontinuous: Human blood group & Plant leaf width; Continuous: Human height & Plant petal number
Discontinuous: Human lobed/lobeless ears & Plant seed coat texture; Continuous: Human body mass & Plant stem length
Discontinuous: Human height & Plant stem length; Continuous: Human eye colour & Plant flower colour
Discontinuous: Human mass & Plant root length; Continuous: Human blood group & Plant leaf number

questions.question: A class is planning to collect primary data on variation. Group A decides to record the tongue-rolling ability of 50 students, while Group B decides to measure the hand span of the same 50 students. Which of the following represents the correct method for collecting and preparing to record these primary data types?
options: Group A must use a ruler to get continuous values, while Group B must tally categories like 'can' and 'cannot'.
Group A should record 'can roll' or 'cannot roll' as tally categories, while Group B should use a measuring tape to record hand spans in centimetres.
Both groups must record their data using exact millimetre measurements to ensure high accuracy for both discontinuous and continuous variation.
Group A should plot a line graph during data collection, while Group B should plot a pie chart directly on their clipboards.

questions.question: A biology student has collected the body lengths of 150 adult woodlice. Why is a histogram or a line graph more appropriate for displaying this data than a bar chart?
options: Because body length is continuous data that can take any value, requiring continuous intervals along the horizontal axis rather than discrete categories.
Because a histogram allows each individual woodlouse to be plotted as a separate, distinct bar with gaps between them.
Because discontinuous data like woodlouse length must be shown with lines to highlight the gaps between different species.
Because a line graph is only used when the variable being measured has fewer than five possible categories.

questions.question: When plotting a histogram for the heights of 200 sunflower plants, what is a crucial rule that must be followed regarding the horizontal axis and the bars?
options: Each sunflower height must be plotted as a separate bar, leaving a distinct gap between every bar to show individual variation.
The horizontal axis must be divided into continuous, equal-width intervals (bins), and the bars must touch to show the continuous nature of the data.
The bars should be ordered from tallest to shortest, with the width of each bar representing the number of sunflowers in that category.
The horizontal axis must list individual sunflower names or labels, with the bars remaining separate to prevent overlapping data.

questions.question: Examine the description of a histogram displaying the shell diameters of a population of garden snails. The histogram shows a bell-shaped curve, with the tallest bars in the middle range (1.8 cm to 2.2 cm) and very short bars at the extreme ends (1.0 cm and 3.0 cm). What does this distribution tell us about the population?
options: Most snails in the population have either extremely small or extremely large shell diameters.
The population consists of two entirely separate species that do not overlap in size.
Most snails have a shell diameter close to the average, with fewer individuals showing extreme values at either end.
The snail shells grow in discrete steps, meaning no snails have diameters between 2.0 cm and 2.1 cm.

questions.question: A clone of a plant is divided into two parts. One part is grown in nutrient-rich soil with plenty of light, and it grows tall with many leaves. The other part is grown in poor soil with low light, and it remains short with few leaves. What does this experiment demonstrate about continuous variation in plant height?
options: Plant height is determined solely by the genetic information inherited from the parent plant.
Continuous variation, like plant height, is influenced by both genetic factors and environmental conditions.
The environment can permanently alter the genetic code of the plant clone to make it short.
Continuous variation is unaffected by lifestyle or environment, and the differences observed were due to random mutations.

questions.question: You are tasked with representing data collected on the ABO blood groups of 80 students. Why is a bar chart with gaps between the bars the correct way to display this data?
options: Because blood groups represent continuous variation, and the gaps show that the data can take any value between groups.
Because blood groups are discontinuous data consisting of distinct, non-overlapping categories, and the gaps emphasize this separation.
Because a bar chart is only used when the total number of participants is less than 50.
Because the gaps allow the reader to easily estimate the average blood group of the entire class.

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to represent the different feather colours of a poultry flock (brown, white, black, speckled), which of the following practices is correct?
options: The feather colours must be arranged along a numerical scale on the horizontal axis, with the bars touching each other.
The vertical axis must show the categories of feather colours, while the horizontal axis represents the frequency using continuous bins.
The categories (brown, white, black, speckled) should be placed on the horizontal axis with gaps between the bars to show they are discrete categories.
The bars must be plotted as a continuous line graph because feather colour can change gradually over the bird's lifetime.

questions.question: An analyst looks at a bar chart showing the frequency of different pea seed shapes (round or wrinkled) in a harvest. One bar is very tall (round) and the other is short (wrinkled), with a clear gap between them. Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of this chart?
options: The pea seeds show continuous variation, with most seeds being partially round and partially wrinkled.
The chart shows discontinuous variation, where seeds belong to one of two distinct, non-overlapping categories.
The environment has caused the wrinkled peas to gradually transition into round peas over time.
The gap between the bars indicates that there are many peas with intermediate shapes that were not recorded.

questions.question: A person's blood type (A, B, AB, or O) is a classic example of discontinuous variation. Which of the following statements best explains the underlying cause of this variation?
options: It is determined by a combination of a person's diet, physical fitness levels, and genetic inheritance.
It is entirely determined by genetic inheritance and is unaffected by the person's environment, lifestyle, or climate.
It changes gradually throughout a person's life depending on the type of food they eat and the diseases they contract.
It is caused entirely by environmental factors during early development in the womb, with no genetic basis.

questions.question: A pair of golden retrievers mate and produce a litter of puppies. Although the puppies have slight differences, they are unmistakably dogs of the golden retriever breed, rather than cats or foxes. What biological principle does this illustrate?
options: Offspring inherit features only from the environment in which they are raised.
When organisms reproduce, they make offspring of the same kind, maintaining species resemblance.
Offspring are identical clones of the maternal parent due to natural replication.
Species resemblance is determined entirely by the temperature during gestation.

questions.question: In a human family, three siblings all have a mixture of physical features that resemble both their mother and their father, such as their father's nose shape and their mother's eye colour. Why do these family resemblances occur?
options: The siblings inherited all their physical features from a single dominant parent.
The siblings copy the facial expressions and physical habits of their parents after birth.
Offspring inherit genetic features from both parents, leading to a blend of similarities to both parents and one another.
The environment in which the family lives shapes their physical features to look identical over time.

questions.question: How are inherited features, such as natural hair colour or lobed ears, physically passed down from parents to their offspring during reproduction?
options: Through the transmission of proteins directly from the parent's digestive tract to the offspring.
By the passage of DNA, containing genetic instructions, from parents to offspring during fertilisation.
Through the physical environment and climate influencing the developing embryo's skin cells.
By the parents teaching the offspring how to express certain physical traits after birth.

questions.question: A young pine tree is growing on a very windy, exposed cliffside. Over several years, its trunk becomes permanently bent and stunted compared to other pine trees of the same species growing in a sheltered valley. What is the primary cause of this bent trunk feature?
options: A rapid mutation in the tree's DNA caused by the wind, which will be passed to all its seeds.
The lifestyle and environmental forces acting on the tree, modifying its physical growth and shape.
The tree's genetic programming, which was designed to make it bend regardless of where it was planted.
A complete lack of species resemblance due to the high altitude of the cliffside.

questions.question: A farmer breeds two award-winning sheep to produce a lamb, hoping the lamb will be identical to the parents. However, the lamb has a slightly different fleece thickness and a unique pattern of spots on its face. Why is this variation between offspring and parents typical?
options: Because sexual reproduction usually results in variation, meaning offspring are not typically identical to their parents or each other.
Because the lamb's DNA was completely replaced by environmental factors after its birth.
Because sheep do not exhibit species resemblance when bred under controlled farm conditions.
Because the parents' genes were damaged by the breeding process, preventing normal inheritance.

questions.question: Compare the differences between a domestic dog and a grey wolf (two different species) with the differences between a German Shepherd and a Chihuahua (two varieties of the same species). Which of the following general biological rules is correct?
options: Differences within a single species are always far greater than the differences between entirely different species.
Differences between different species are typically greater than the differences within a single species.
There are no measurable physical differences between different species, only within species.
Species resemblance ensures that all species on Earth are identical, meaning variation only exists within families.

questions.question: If you look closely at a field of daisies, you will notice that some have slightly longer petals, some have yellow-green centers, and others have pale yellow centers, even though they all belong to the species Bellis perennis. What is the scientific term for these differences among individuals of the same species?
options: Speciation
Adaptation
Variation
Classification

questions.question: An indoor cat has a small nick in its left ear because it got caught on a wire toy when it was a kitten. Which of the following statements correctly classifies this variation?
options: It is an inherited genetic variation because it changed the shape of the cat's ear permanently.
It is a continuous variation because the size of the nick can be measured on a millimetre scale.
It is an environmental variation caused only by the environment and physical injury, with no genetic basis.
It is a combined variation because the cat's lifestyle interacted with its ear-healing genes to create the nick.

questions.question: A researcher records the blood group (A, B, AB, O) of 100 volunteers. Why is blood group classified as exhibiting discontinuous variation?
options: The data falls into distinct, separate categories with no intermediate values.
The values span a continuous spectrum that changes depending on age.
The trait is gradually altered by dietary habits over a lifetime.
The measurements require a continuous numerical scale such as centimeters.

questions.question: A student measures the mass of 50 acorns gathered from a single oak tree. Which observation best proves that acorn mass shows continuous variation?
options: Acorns fall strictly into two distinct mass categories: light and heavy.
The mass of each acorn is completely unaffected by environmental rainfall.
The masses can take any numerical value within a minimum and maximum range.
Acorn mass is determined solely by a single gene inherited from the parent tree.

questions.question: Consider three plant features: flower petal color (red, white, pink), stem length in centimeters, and presence of thorns (present or absent). Which option correctly classifies these features?
options: Petal color: continuous; Stem length: discontinuous; Thorns: continuous
Petal color: discontinuous; Stem length: continuous; Thorns: discontinuous
Petal color: discontinuous; Stem length: discontinuous; Thorns: continuous
Petal color: continuous; Stem length: continuous; Thorns: discontinuous

questions.question: A class plans to gather primary data on variation within a hedge population. Which method correctly collects primary data for a continuous trait?
options: Counting how many leaves are dark green versus light green.
Ticking boxes to record whether bushes have flowers or no flowers.
Using a millimeter ruler to measure the length of 50 randomly selected leaves.
Asking local residents to vote on their favorite hedge shape.

questions.question: A scientist collects data on the body lengths of 200 adult salmon. Why is a histogram chosen rather than a standard bar chart with spaces between bars to display this data?
options: Histogram bars touch to represent continuous numerical ranges rather than separate categories.
A histogram is only used when data can be grouped into non-numerical word labels.
Standard bar charts are strictly reserved for traits influenced purely by the environment.
Histograms require spaces between bars to show that individual fish are distinct.

questions.question: When plotting continuous plant height data ranging from 10.0 cm to 29.9 cm on a histogram, how should the horizontal axis be constructed?
options: Using separate non-adjacent bars labeled with individual plant names.
Using continuous, equal interval bins such as 10.0–14.9, 15.0–19.9, 20.0–24.9, and 25.0–29.9 with touching bars.
Sorting the plants randomly into two separate bars named 'Short' and 'Tall'.
Leaving wide gaps between each measurement point to highlight missing data.

questions.question: A histogram showing human foot lengths in a school displays a symmetric bell-shaped distribution centered around 25 cm. What correct conclusion can be drawn from this graph?
options: Foot length is a discontinuous trait controlled by a single environmental factor.
Most individuals have foot lengths near the average, with fewer individuals at extreme lengths.
Every student in the school has a foot length of exactly 25 cm.
Foot length is divided into discrete categories with no individuals measuring between 24 cm and 26 cm.

questions.question: Two genetically identical cuttings from the same plant are grown in different soils. One grows tall with abundant leaves, while the other stays short with few leaves. What does this demonstrate about continuous variation?
options: Continuous traits are determined exclusively by inherited DNA sequences.
Environmental conditions can significantly influence traits that display continuous variation.
Genetics plays no role whatsoever in determining plant growth height.
Cutting plants causes discontinuous mutations in growth patterns.

questions.question: A student wants to present data showing the number of pupils with attached versus unattached earlobes. Which graph design is appropriate for this discontinuous trait?
options: A histogram with touching bars to show smooth numerical transitions.
A line graph connecting the data points with a line of best fit.
A bar chart with separate bars and gaps between them to represent distinct categories.
A scatter plot showing earlobe area plotted against pupil age.

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to show the frequency of different natural hair colors in a classroom, which rule must be followed?
options: The bars must touch each other because hair color is a continuous numerical variable.
The vertical axis must show color categories while the horizontal axis shows frequency.
Category labels go on the horizontal axis with equal-width bars separated by gaps.
Data points should be connected with a continuous trend line.

questions.question: A bar chart of human tongue-rolling ability shows 18 students in the 'Can Roll' bar and 6 students in the 'Cannot Roll' bar. How should this graph be correctly interpreted?
options: Tongue rolling is a continuous feature where students gradually improve with practice.
The feature shows discontinuous variation, splitting the population into distinct categories.
The 6 non-rollers will develop rolling ability if their diet changes.
There are intermediate categories of partial rollers present between the main bars.

questions.question: An athlete moves to a sunny region and alters their diet, increasing muscle mass and skin pigmentation. However, their ABO blood group remains type O. Why does blood group remain unchanged?
options: Discontinuous traits like blood group are determined solely by genetic factors and are unaffected by environment or lifestyle.
Blood group changes so slowly that it takes several decades of lifestyle changes to alter.
Sunlight counteracts dietary shifts, preventing alterations in blood proteins.
Muscle mass gain neutralizes genetic shifts in blood antigens.

questions.question: When male and female robins reproduce, their eggs always hatch into robins rather than sparrows or blackbirds. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Environmental adaptation
Species resemblance
Discontinuous mutation
Acquired variation

questions.question: A puppy has coat coloring similar to its mother and ear shape identical to its father. What explains this family resemblance?
options: The puppy learned these physical traits by observing its parents after birth.
The puppy inherited genetic features from both parents during reproduction.
The mother and father modified their own DNA after the puppy was born.
The puppy's physical traits were shaped entirely by the temperature of its nest.

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains how inherited features are passed from parents to offspring during reproduction?
options: Parents pass physical traits directly through protein molecules in food.
Offspring absorb environmental habits from parents, which alter physical features.
Genetic information stored in DNA is passed from parents to offspring.
Nerve signals during early growth copy the parents' physical structures.

questions.question: A cat loses part of its tail in an accident and gains weight after moving indoors. Which statement correctly describes these features?
options: They are inherited features that will be passed to future kittens via DNA.
They are discontinuous genetic traits caused by gene replication.
They are caused by environment and lifestyle and will not be inherited by offspring.
They are species-level characteristics present in all domestic cats from birth.

questions.question: Two non-identical human brothers share the same parents and environment, yet one has blue eyes and is tall, while the other has brown eyes and is shorter. Why does variation exist between these siblings?
options: Offspring inherit identical DNA combinations from parents, but one sibling mutated.
Reproduction results in variation between offspring, so they are not usually identical to parents or each other.
Siblings are classified into different species based on birth order.
Family members only differ if they live in entirely different geographic regions.

questions.question: Comparing the differences between a domestic dog and a red fox to the differences between two individual German Shepherd dogs, which statement is true?
options: Differences within a species are greater than differences between different species.
Differences between different species are greater than differences within the same species.
There are no measurable differences between individuals of the same species.
Differences between species are caused purely by lifestyle, whereas internal species traits are purely genetic.

questions.question: A farmer observes that within a flock of 100 sheep of the same breed, individuals have slightly different horn shapes, body masses, and wool textures. What term describes these differences among individuals of the same species?
options: Speciation
Variation
Classification
Inheritance

questions.question: An individual's potential body mass is influenced by genes inherited from parents, but their actual adult body mass is heavily affected by daily food intake and physical activity. This trait is an example of variation caused by:
options: Only environmental factors, as genetics has no influence on body mass.
Only genetic factors, as lifestyle cannot alter inherited mass potential.
A combination of genetic and environmental/lifestyle factors.
Discontinuous genetic mutation caused by dietary chemicals.
